key_insight: HVAF-sprayed Tribaloy-400 forms a denser, more protective oxide layer than detonation-sprayed T-400, giving better resistance to molten-salt corrosion at 500 °C.
engineering_relevance: For solar thermal energy storage containers, HVAF coating of T-400 on ASTM A516 steel offers a more durable option to limit corrosion, salt ingress, and spallation during long service at high temperature.
method: Compared HVAF and detonation spraying of Tribaloy-400 on ASTM A516 steel.
Exposed coated samples to 60% NaNO3–40% KNO3 solar salt at 500 °C for up to 1000 h.
Evaluated phase evolution, elemental mapping, SEM microstructure, mass gain, and spallation behavior.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports that HVAF retained a uniform Cr–Mo–Si–O enriched surface with minimal salt penetration after 1000 h, while DS showed deeper ingress, higher mass gain, and more spallation.
watch_item: Results are specific to one salt composition, one substrate, and 500 °C exposure, so performance may differ under cycling, other salts, or longer field conditions.
paper_title: Hot corrosion behavior of thermal sprayed using HVAF and DS techniques with Tribaloy-400 coatings for solar energy storage container
